topic.commandRouting.title: How a Command Is Routed
topic.commandRouting.body:
Simple commands like "turn off the kitchen light" don't need a full AI model. When command handling is on, Phoenix tries cheaper ways first.

## The order Phoenix tries {#order}

1. Home Assistant's sentence matching, in every installed Assist language. It runs in your home and costs nothing.
2. The decision provider, if you use one. It handles the commands sentence matching missed.
3. Your AI model, for everything else, just as without command handling.

Once a step carries out a command, the later steps aren't used.

Related: [Decision provider](guide:window.settingsProviders#decision-provider)

## When it applies {#when}

You turn command handling on separately for [Agent Chat](guide:window.settingsChat#chat-commands) and the [Voice Agent](guide:window.settingsHome#voice-commands).

It only applies to plain text messages. Messages for Home Companion keys always go straight to the companion.

## Follow-up messages {#follow-ups}

The first message in a conversation can go to the decision provider. A follow-up only goes there with a TypeSafe / JEV model, in a language the model supports. Otherwise it goes to your AI model.

## Limits {#limits}

The decision provider has a time limit for each request, and an optional hourly limit. If either is reached, the command goes to your AI model, so nothing goes unanswered.

Related: [Connection settings](guide:window.settingsProviders#decision-connection)

## Seeing the effect {#effect}

Routing statistics count how each message was handled, so you can see what command handling saves you.

Related: [Reading the statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics)

topic.homeAssistantFeatures.title: Voice Agent, AI Task or Assist Tool Provider

topic.killSwitch.title: What the Kill Switch Stops
topic.killSwitch.body:
The kill switch cuts off every way an AI can reach your home through Phoenix. It doesn't undo actions that already happened.

## What stops {#stops}

- External apps connected over MCP are refused. Requests already running stop at their next check.
- Agent Chat closes, and can't be opened again.
- The Voice Agent only replies that it's unavailable.
- The AI Task entity becomes unavailable.
- Assist Tool Provider offers no tools.
- Approving a waiting request cancels it instead.

## What keeps working {#keeps}

This panel keeps working, so you can review what happened and turn the switch off again. You can still edit MESA profiles, and the in-context profile buttons stay.

## After a restart {#restart}

If the switch is on when Home Assistant starts, Phoenix doesn't open its connections at all. Turning the switch off opens them, without a restart.

Related: [Emergency kill switch](guide:window.settingsSafety#kill-switch)

topic.routingStatistics.title: Reading Routing Statistics
topic.routingStatistics.body:
Routing statistics show how often Phoenix carried out a command without your AI model, and what the rest cost. Agent Chat and the Voice Agent are counted separately.

## The headline {#headline}

The percentage at the top is the share of messages handled by sentence matching or the decision provider. The higher it is, the fewer full model turns you paid for.

## The counts {#counts}

Each message is counted once, by its outcome. If a message used your AI model at any point, it counts as sent to it.

- **{{label:routingStats.local}}**: Home Assistant's sentence matching carried it out.
- **{{label:routingStats.decision}}**: the decision provider carried it out.
- **{{label:routingStats.provider}}**: your AI model handled it.
- **{{label:routingStats.pending}}**: waiting for your approval.
- **{{label:routingStats.failed}}** and **{{label:routingStats.cancelled}}**: messages that didn't finish.

A message sent to your AI model can also fail or be cancelled, so the rows don't always add up.

## Tokens {#tokens}

The token rows total what the decision provider and your AI model reported using. Providers don't always report usage. Requests without a report are counted below the totals.

## Refresh and reset {#refresh-and-reset}

**{{label:common.refresh}}** loads the latest counts. **{{label:routingStats.reset}}** sets this window's counts back to zero, after you confirm. Messages still in progress aren't counted after a reset.

Counts are saved every 30 seconds and survive a restart. Deleting core data in [Data Management](guide:window.settingsSafety#wipe-core) clears them.

window.chatRoutingStatistics.title: {{label:routingStats.chatWindow}}
window.chatRoutingStatistics.body:
Counts how Agent Chat's messages were handled since the last reset: by Home Assistant's sentence matching, the decision provider, or your AI model. Open it with **{{label:routingStats.show}}** in the {{label:settings.agentcliCard}} window, or from **{{label:workspace.options}}**.

Every Agent Chat message counts, even with **{{label:routing.enableChat}}** off. AI Task and external apps aren't counted.

Related: [Reading the statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics), [Handle chat commands directly](guide:window.settingsChat#chat-commands)

window.settingsChat.title: {{label:settings.agentcliCard}}
window.settingsChat.body:
Settings for Agent Chat, Phoenix's own chat window. Choose the access key, account and model in the chat window itself.

## {{label:routing.enableChat}} {#chat-commands}

Carries out simple commands, such as turning on a light, without your AI model. Phoenix uses Home Assistant's own sentence matching, in every installed Assist language. Off by default.

If a decision provider is in use, it handles the commands sentence matching misses. Everything else goes to your AI model as usual.

This doesn't apply to Home Companion keys, or to messages that aren't plain text.

Related: [Decision provider](guide:window.settingsProviders#decision-provider), [How a command is routed](guide:topic.commandRouting)

## {{label:settings.agentcliGlobalLabel}} {#chat-global}

Lets Agent Chat open on any Home Assistant page, not just in this panel. Press Shift+A to show or hide it. On by default.

Shift+A needs keyboard shortcuts turned on in your Home Assistant profile. In this panel, Shift+A works even when this setting is off.

A change takes effect the next time the page fully loads. The **{{label:settings.killSwitchCard}}** closes Agent Chat everywhere.

## {{label:settings.agentcliScrollbackLabel}} {#chat-memory}

How many lines of the conversation Phoenix sends with each new message: 0 to 5,000 (default 100).

Older turns are dropped whole, and the newest turn is always sent. At 0, no earlier turns are sent. More history gives the model more context, but each message costs more.

## {{label:settings.agentcliStepsLabel}} {#chat-steps}

The maximum tool steps the model can take for one message: 3 to 100 (default 20). Steps spent fixing a malformed tool call count too.

At the limit, Agent Chat asks whether to continue. The Voice Agent and AI Task use the same limit, but stop instead.

## {{label:settings.conversationStyle}} {#chat-style}

How replies sound: {{label:settings.styleDirect}} (default), {{label:settings.styleWarm}}, {{label:settings.styleCalmGuide}}, {{label:settings.styleLively}} or {{label:settings.styleTechnical}}. This changes the wording, not what Phoenix does.

## {{label:settings.detailLevel}} {#chat-detail}

How much replies say: {{label:settings.detailConcise}} (default), {{label:settings.detailBalanced}} or {{label:settings.detailDetailed}}.

## {{label:settings.homeFocused}} {#chat-home-focused}

Asks the model to stick to your home and decline other subjects. Off by default.

This is a preference, not a security control: the model is asked, not forced. Its access key decides what it can actually do.

Related: [Access Keys](guide:workspace.accessKeys)

## {{label:routingStats.title}} {#chat-statistics}

**{{label:routingStats.show}}** opens a window that counts how Agent Chat's messages were handled: by sentence matching, the decision provider, or your AI model.

Related: [Reading the statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics)

window.settingsProviders.title: {{label:workspace.aiProviders}}
window.settingsProviders.body:
Add the AI accounts Phoenix uses. Each account needs an API key or, for a local model, a server address.

Agent Chat, the Voice Agent and AI Task each use one of these accounts, with a model you choose.

## Accounts {#provider-accounts}

Lists every account with its provider and default model. Select an account to show its options, and select it again to hide them.

If something is wrong with an account, such as a model the provider no longer offers, a warning appears in its options.

### {{label:settings.accountChangeModel}} {#change-model}

Choose from the models the provider offers. Models that can't use tools are greyed out, because Phoenix needs tools to act.

**{{label:settings.agentcliModelAuto}}** always uses the provider's newest suitable model. If you pick a model yourself, Phoenix keeps it until the provider retires it, then switches to its successor.

When **{{label:settings.agentcliVerifyOptions}}** is on, saving also checks which options the model supports. This uses a little API credit.

### {{label:settings.accountRefreshModels}} {#refresh-models}

Reloads the provider's list of models. This uses no tokens. On a local Ollama server, Phoenix asks about each model in turn.

### {{label:settings.accountCheckOptions}} {#check-options}

Finds out which effort levels the model supports and whether it can read images, by sending it a few one-token requests.

This uses a little credit, so Phoenix asks first. Hover over the button to see when it last ran.

### Removing an account {#remove-account}

Removing an account deletes its stored key. You confirm in place first.

If the Voice Agent or AI Task used the account, they lose it, and Phoenix removes the Assist assistant and AI Task entity it created for them.

Related: [Voice Agent](guide:window.settingsHome#voice-agent), [AI Task](guide:window.settingsHome#ai-task)

## Adding an account {#provider-add}

1. Select **{{label:settings.addAccount}}** on the toolbar to show the providers.
2. Pick a provider and fill in its fields.
3. Select **{{label:settings.agentcliValidate}}**. This checks the details with the provider, but saves nothing yet.
4. Choose a model, or keep **{{label:settings.agentcliModelAuto}}**, then select **{{label:settings.agentcliDone}}**.

If you change a field after validating, validate again. Phoenix checks the details once more before it saves the account.

### What each provider asks for {#provider-kinds}

Most providers need only an API key. Some also need to know where your account is:

- OpenAI, Grok, Kimi, Mistral AI and MiniMax: the region your key was issued for.
- Xiaomi MiMo: pay as you go, or your Token Plan region.
- Tencent Cloud TokenHub: the site that issued your key. A key works only on that site.
- OpenCode: the Zen or Console route. You can add a key on one route only.
- Z.ai: Standard API, Coding Plan or China. You can save the same key once for each plan.
- Qwen: your workspace's base URL, a public HTTPS address, as well as the API key.
- Ollama (local): your Ollama server's address. Home Assistant connects to it, so use an address the Home Assistant host can reach.

OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Kimi, Mistral AI, OpenRouter and Z.ai accept at most 128 tools per request. Phoenix gives them a smaller set to start with, and loads more when the model asks.

## {{label:settings.catalogChecks}} {#catalog-checks}

Phoenix rereads each account's model list from time to time. This keeps the lists up to date, so **{{label:settings.agentcliModelAuto}}** can move to a newer model.

### {{label:settings.providerChecksLabel}} {#provider-checks}

Once an hour, Phoenix rereads any model list older than the period below. This uses no tokens. On by default.

When it's off, Phoenix still reads a list when it needs one: for a new account, when a provider reports a missing model, and when you switch to **{{label:settings.agentcliModelAuto}}**.

### {{label:settings.providerChecksHoursLabel}} {#provider-checks-hours}

How old a model list can get before Phoenix rereads it: 6 to 720 hours (default 24). Greyed out while checks are off.

## {{label:routing.providerSection}} {#decision-provider}

A decision provider is a small, fast model that carries out simple commands, so your main AI model doesn't have to. It saves the cost and the wait of a full model turn.

It works with **{{label:routing.enableChat}}** and **{{label:routing.enableVoice}}**. Phoenix tries Home Assistant's own sentence matching first, and the decision provider handles the commands sentence matching misses.

Phoenix offers one decision provider, TypeSafe / JEV. Add your account here and select the model.

To use it, choose its account. Choose **{{label:routing.noProvider}}** to stop using it; commands then rely on sentence matching alone.

Related: [How a command is routed](guide:topic.commandRouting)

## {{label:routing.connectionSettings}} {#decision-connection}

These limits apply while a decision provider is in use.

### {{label:routing.decisionBudget}} {#decision-timeout}

How long Phoenix waits for the decision provider: 250 to 30,000 milliseconds (default 5,000). If the prompt times out, the request goes to your main AI model as usual.

### {{label:routing.requestLimit}} {#decision-request-limit}

The maximum decision requests Phoenix can send per hour. Set to 0 (default) for no limit. Every use of the decision provider increases the count, including failed requests.

When the limit is reached, commands go to your main AI model until the hour ends.

window.settingsSafety.title: {{label:workspace.safety}}
window.settingsSafety.body:
Stop Phoenix in an emergency, choose how strictly MESA protects your devices, and delete Phoenix's data.

## {{label:settings.killSwitchCard}} {#kill-switch}

**{{label:settings.killSwitchDisableLabel}}** immediately cuts off every way an AI can reach your home through Phoenix, with no confirmation. Turn it off to restore access. No restart is needed.

While it's on, a warning button on the toolbar leads back to this switch.

Related: [What the kill switch stops](guide:topic.killSwitch)

## {{label:settings.mesaModeLabel}} {#mesa-mode}

What MESA, Phoenix's device safety layer, does when an action breaks a profile's rules. Default: {{label:settings.mesaModeAdvisory}}.

- {{label:settings.mesaModeOff}}: MESA is skipped, and every action is allowed.
- {{label:settings.mesaModeAdvisory}}: most rules only warn. Privacy rules, read-only devices and profiles set to enforce still block.
- {{label:settings.mesaModeEnforced}}: forbidden actions are blocked, and actions that need confirmation wait for your approval.

Devices without a MESA profile follow a built-in baseline: lights are allowed, locks and alarm panels are forbidden, and everything else needs approval. Add profiles before you rely on {{label:settings.mesaModeEnforced}}.

Related: [MESA](guide:workspace.mesa)

## {{label:settings.dataCard}} {#data-management}

Deletes Phoenix's data. Choose what to delete, select **{{label:settings.wipeSubmit}}**, then type WIPE to confirm. The page reloads afterwards.

You can't undo a wipe. It's refused while an approved request is still running.

### {{label:settings.wipeCoreLabel}} {#wipe-core}

Deletes every access key, pending approval and entity hint, and resets all settings to their defaults. This also turns off the kill switch.

It also deletes the audit log, Conversation Log, change history, routing statistics and rate-limit counts, and removes the voice assistant Phoenix created.

### {{label:settings.wipeProvidersLabel}} {#wipe-providers}

Deletes every AI and decision provider account, with their keys. The Voice Agent, AI Task and command routing lose their accounts, and Phoenix removes the voice assistant it created.

### {{label:settings.wipeMesaLabel}} {#wipe-mesa}

Deletes every MESA profile, at every level, and the suggestions you dismissed. Off by default, so a wipe keeps your device rules unless you choose this.

window.voiceRoutingStatistics.title: {{label:routingStats.voiceWindow}}
window.voiceRoutingStatistics.body:
Counts how voice commands were handled since the last reset: by Home Assistant's sentence matching, the decision provider, or your AI model. Open it with **{{label:routingStats.show}}** on the {{label:settings.voiceCard}} tab, or from **{{label:workspace.options}}**.

Related: [Reading the statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics), [Handle voice commands directly](guide:window.settingsHome#voice-commands)

wizard.access.title: Granting Access to One Light
wizard.access.body:
A new key can reach nothing until you grant it something. Grant one light you can see, so the test shows everything working.

Expand the light group and choose **W** on a light, for read and write access. A grant on a device covers its entities. A grant on the whole domain covers every light, including ones added later.

If this Home Assistant has no lights, **{{label:wizard.showAllDevices}}** lists every domain. You can grant more later in the {{label:accessKeys.permissionsTree}}.

wizard.accessKey.title: Naming the Access Key
wizard.accessKey.body:
The agent uses this access key to connect to Phoenix. The key's name appears in the audit log and in approvals, so pick a name that says which agent uses it.

An expiry date ends the key automatically, and you can't change it once the key exists. **{{label:wizard.createAccessKey}}** creates the key. If you're connecting an external app, its secret value appears in the Connect step.

wizard.choose.title: How Your Agent Connects
wizard.choose.body:
Phoenix is installed. This wizard sets up your first agent, and finishes with a test you can watch.

- **{{label:wizard.choiceChatTitle}}** runs the agent in a chat window inside Home Assistant. You need an API key from a model provider, or the address of a local Ollama server.
- **{{label:wizard.choiceAppTitle}}** connects an MCP app you already use, such as Claude Code or an IDE, with a bearer access key.

Either way, the agent gets its own access key, and the next steps decide what that key can do. You can set up more agents later with **{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}**.

wizard.connect.title: Connecting an External App
wizard.connect.body:
Choose your app to get the exact command or configuration, with this key's secret value filled in. Copy it now: Phoenix only stores a hash of the key, and can't show the value again. If you lose it, rotate the key to get a new one.

**{{label:wizard.testConnection}}** waits for the app's first request. **{{label:wizard.connectLater}}** finishes now and leaves the test for later.

wizard.done.title: Your Agent Is Ready
wizard.done.body:
Your key is ready. In [Access Keys](guide:workspace.accessKeys) you can change its persona, capabilities and permissions. **{{label:workspace.keyActions}}** rotates or revokes it.

The agent can reach only what its key grants, and changes set to confirm wait for you in [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals).

wizard.persona.title: Choosing a Persona
wizard.persona.body:
A persona is a starting set of capabilities: which kinds of tools the agent can use, and which ones wait for your approval first.

The preselected persona is the safe choice for a first test. If you already know the agent's job, pick another. You can change single capabilities later in [Access Keys](guide:workspace.accessKeys).

A persona never decides which devices the agent can reach. You choose that two steps from now.

wizard.provider.title: Setting Up the Model Provider
wizard.provider.body:
Agent Chat sends the conversation to the model provider you choose, using your own account.

Pick an account you've already added, or add one: choose the provider, enter the API key or Ollama server address, and validate it. Nothing is saved until it validates.

**{{label:wizard.tryNow}}** clears Agent Chat's conversation and opens it with the new key, with a test question already typed in.

wizard.test.title: Testing the Connection
wizard.test.body:
Send the suggested prompt from your app. When Phoenix sees the app's first request, **{{label:wizard.next}}** becomes available.

If nothing arrives, check that the app has loaded its new configuration (some apps need a restart), and that the address and key match the Connect step.

wizard.try.title: Trying Agent Chat
wizard.try.body:
Agent Chat is open, with a test question typed in. Send it, and watch the agent work with the light you granted.

The wizard closes when you send your first message. Changes that need your approval wait in [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals).

workspace.accessKeys.title: Access Keys
workspace.accessKeys.body:
Each agent connects to Phoenix with its own access key. The key decides what that agent can do in Home Assistant.

- **{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}** walks you through creating a key and connecting an app.
- Select a key in the list to show its **{{label:accessKeys.cardPersona}}**, **{{label:accessKeys.cardCapabilities}}**, **{{label:workspace.keySettings}}** and **{{label:accessKeys.permissionsTree}}** windows.
- **{{label:accessKeys.permissionSummary}}** sums up everything the key can reach.
- Until you select a key, only the list is shown. The key stays selected when you come back from another workspace.
- Each window grows to fit its content, so the workspace scrolls instead of the windows.
- The **{{label:accessKeys.permissionsTree}}** keeps up with Home Assistant as entities, devices, areas and labels change. **{{label:selectBy.menu}}** narrows it to one area, label or integration.
- **{{label:workspace.keyActions}}** on the toolbar renames, rotates or revokes the selected key.
- **{{label:accessKeys.showArchived}}** opens **{{label:accessKeys.archivedTitle}}** under the list, with the revoked and expired keys. It closes when you select a key.
- If you try another persona, choosing **{{label:personas.custom.label}}** again brings back the key's custom capabilities, until you close the panel.

When a capability is set to confirm, the agent's changes go to [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals) first, and nothing runs until you decide.

workspace.approvals.title: Approvals
workspace.approvals.body:
When a capability is set to confirm, the agent's change waits here for your decision. Nothing runs until you decide.

- **{{label:shell.tabApprovals}}** lists the requests. Use **{{label:approvals.show}}** to see **{{label:approvals.tabPending}}**, **{{label:approvals.tabHistory}}** or one outcome. Choose a request to see it in **{{label:workspace.review}}**.
- **{{label:workspace.review}}** shows exactly what would change. **{{label:approvals.approve}}** runs the request. **{{label:approvals.reject}}** refuses it, and you can tell the agent why before you confirm.
- **{{label:workspace.requestDetails}}**, on the toolbar once you choose a request, shows its access key, capability, inputs and recorded result, under Review.
- The list updates itself, so there's nothing to refresh. Restarting Home Assistant cancels any requests still waiting, and marks them in the list, since nothing is waiting for their results any more.
- **{{label:approvals.selectMultiple}}** approves several requests at once, in the order shown. Use it for requests you already know.

Configuration that agents change is recorded in [Changes](guide:workspace.changes), where you can put back an earlier version.

workspace.changes.title: Changes
workspace.changes.body:
Changes keeps a version history of the configuration agents change: automations, scripts, scenes, integrations, helpers and dashboards.

- Choose a change to compare the configuration before and after it in **{{label:workspace.comparison}}**. **{{label:workspace.itemHistory}}**, on the toolbar, lists the item's other changes.
- **{{label:changes.restore}}** puts back a saved Before or After version, after you confirm. The restore is recorded too, so you can undo it the same way.

workspace.logs.title: Logs
workspace.logs.body:
Logs shows what reached Phoenix and what agents said.

- **{{label:shell.tabAudit}}** records requests to Phoenix, with their outcome, access key, method and resource.
- **{{label:conversations.title}}** keeps recorded agent conversations, such as Agent Chat sessions.
- Select a record in either log to read it in full in **{{label:workspace.logDetails}}**.

Choose what's recorded, and for how long, in [{{label:workspace.logsNotifications}}](guide:window.settingsLogs).

workspace.mesa.title: MESA
workspace.mesa.body:
MESA describes what each device or entity is, so Phoenix can handle it safely. A profile can make a device need confirmation, or put it off-limits, whatever an access key allows.

- A profile can cover a domain, an integration, an area, a device or a single entity. **{{label:workspace.mesaProfiles}}** lists them all. Choose one to open it in **{{label:workspace.profileEditor}}**, or start a new one with **{{label:mesa.addProfile}}**.
- **{{label:mesa.suggestTitle}}** proposes profiles for devices Phoenix recognizes. Nothing is applied until you choose one, check it in the editor and save it. **{{label:mesa.dismiss}}** removes a suggestion from the list.
- **{{label:workspace.advisory}}** appears only while MESA has a finding: an automation it could only partly inspect, a trigger that doesn't match its declaration, or a profile whose target is gone.
- Dismissing a finding doesn't change any profile. **{{label:mesa.restoreNotices}}** in the MESA Actions menu shows them again.
- Until **{{label:settings.mesaModeLabel}}** in [Settings](guide:window.settingsSafety#mesa-mode) is **{{label:settings.mesaModeEnforced}}**, most restrictions only warn.

workspace.my.title: My Workspace
workspace.my.body:
My Workspace gathers the windows you use most from the other workspaces.

- **{{label:workspace.addToMy}}** in a window's menu adds it here. It stays in its own workspace too, and both copies show the same selection.
- Each new window goes in the next place: beside the first, then a row or column at a time.
- Closing a window here removes it. To bring it back, add it again from its own workspace.
- **{{label:workspace.verticalScrolling}}**, in any window's menu here, lets the workspace grow taller than the screen and scroll. Every window gets back its earlier height, or its usual height.
- With it on, drag the border under a window, or the workspace's bottom edge, to make it taller. With it off, every window shrinks to fit the screen.
- **{{label:workspace.restoreOriginal}}** empties My Workspace.
- **{{label:shell.agentChat}}** docks here from its own menu. While another workspace is shown, Chat floats over it, and it comes back here when you return. **{{label:agentchat.floatChat}}** undocks it.

workspace.settings.title: Settings
workspace.settings.body:
Settings that apply to all of Phoenix, in six windows. Select a window, or one of its settings, to read about it here.

- [{{label:workspace.aiProviders}}](guide:window.settingsProviders): the AI accounts Phoenix uses, and the optional {{label:routing.providerSection}}.
- [{{label:settings.agentcliCard}}](guide:window.settingsChat): how Agent Chat behaves.
- [{{label:workspace.homeAssistant}}](guide:window.settingsHome): Phoenix in Home Assistant's voice, AI Task and Assist features.
- [{{label:workspace.safety}}](guide:window.settingsSafety): the {{label:settings.killSwitchCard}}, MESA enforcement and {{label:settings.dataCard}}.
- [{{label:workspace.logsNotifications}}](guide:window.settingsLogs): what's recorded, and when Home Assistant notifies you.
- [{{label:workspace.general}}](guide:window.settingsGeneral): language, theme, optional features and version.

To find a setting by name, use **{{label:workspace.findSetting}}** on the toolbar. It opens the window the setting is in.

Changes save automatically. Settings apply to every access key and every Home Assistant user, except {{label:settings.languageLabel}} and {{label:settings.themeLabel}}, which apply to this browser only.
